definitions.explanation: A collective term for fresh fruits and vegetables, especially in commercial and market contexts. Literally 'green goods.'

examples.japanese: {青果|せいか}コーナーで{野菜|やさい}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I picked out vegetables in the produce section.

examples.japanese: この{市場|いちば}は{青果|せいか}の{品揃|しなぞろ}えが{豊富|ほうふ}だ。
examples.english: This market has a rich selection of fresh produce.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{青果|せいか}{店|てん}がオープンして、{新鮮|しんせん}な{地元|じもと}の{野菜|やさい}や{果物|くだもの}が{手|て}に{入|はい}るようになった。
examples.english: A new produce shop opened near the station, making it possible to get fresh local vegetables and fruits.

notes:
A compound of {青|せい} (green, fresh) and {果|か} (fruit). Used primarily in commercial and business contexts rather than casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {青果|せいか}{店|てん} (produce shop, greengrocer)
- {青果|せいか}{市場|しじょう} (produce market, wholesale fruit and vegetable market)
- {青果|せいか}コーナー (produce section in a supermarket)
- {青果|せいか}{売|う}り{場|ば} (produce sales area)

In supermarkets, the produce section is typically labeled {青果|せいか} alongside {精肉|せいにく} (meat), {鮮魚|せんぎょ} (fresh fish), and {惣菜|そうざい} (deli/prepared foods). In everyday conversation, people usually say {野菜|やさい}と{果物|くだもの} rather than {青果|せいか}.
